country.comment: Primary field study conducted in Foumbot municipality, Noun Division, West Region, Cameroon.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title & Abstract; PDF p. 3, Study Area

effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative analysis consists of descriptive frequencies (n = 100) and a univariate chi-square goodness-of-fit test on water source distribution; no multivariable regression or causal treatment effect is estimated, while institutional/policy mechanisms are documented via utility fee records, descriptive ratings, and qualitative interviews/observations.
effect_estimate.value: Among 100 surveyed participants in Foumbot, only 8% rely on Camwater piped taps, compared with 36% relying on streams, 24% on wells, 18% on boreholes, and 14% on springs; a chi-square goodness-of-fit test confirms uneven water source reliance (chi-square = 22.8, df = 4, critical value = 9.488, p = 0.0001388). High Camwater installation fees (117.245 FCFA for 20 m pipe and 176.632 FCFA for 40 m pipe at 0-5 m distance; 192.850 FCFA for 20 m pipe and 268.013 FCFA for 40 m pipe at 50 m distance) and tariffs starting at 293/364 FCFA per m3 deter connections (total Camwater users rose slowly from 2,076 in 2015 to 2,772 in 2021), while 52% of respondents rated Camwater management as poor and 26% as below average (16% average, 6% satisfactory, 0% exceptional). Qualitatively, centralized decree-based governance lacking comprehensive water legislation or enforcement follow-up, inconsistent institutional frameworks, minimal community participation, uninspected broken pipes, inadequate storage/pipe capacity, and power outages cause irregular tap supply and weeks-long water cuts.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 9-10, Tables 1-2 & Fig. 4; PDF pp. 11-13, Results & Chi-Square Analysis Results

mechanism_certainty.comment: Mixed-methods cross-sectional case study (capped at 2 by design ceiling) that directly documents local utility connection fee schedules, subscriber counts, respondent evaluations of Camwater management, uninspected pipe infrastructure, minimal community engagement, and unimplemented centralized decrees via primary fieldwork and utility records, without causal/quasi-experimental identification.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 4-5, Materials and Methods; PDF pp. 10-12, Results

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines high Camwater connection/installation fees and water tariffs deterring connections (BURDEN, fees), minimal community engagement and stakeholder participation in water management (participation), fragmented/inconsistent institutional frameworks across multiple ministries, council, and Camwater (institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination), land-use/catchment and capacity planning gaps (planning), and unimplemented government decrees, lack of infrastructure inspection/accountability, pollution control gaps, and penalties vs. subsidies for household latrines (ENFORCEMENT, sanction).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, ENFORCEMENT, fees, participation, institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination, planning, sanction
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 1-2, Abstract & Introduction; PDF pp. 6-8, Stakeholders; PDF pp. 10-14, Results & Conclusion

outcome_flags.comment: Measures household water source reliance across JMP ladder categories (water_access), Camwater piped tap use and subscriber counts (formal_connection), water tariffs and prohibitive installation fees (affordability), irregular tap supply, rationing, and multi-week water cuts (service_reliability, service_continuity), water production/consumption volumes and shortages (service_quantity), and perceived/observed water contamination and waterborne disease risk (service_quality). Sanitation (latrines) is mentioned only as a policy recommendation on PDF pp. 1 and 14 rather than empirically measured.
outcome_flags.value: water_access, formal_connection, affordability, service_reliability, service_continuity, service_quantity, service_quality
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 5, Methods; PDF pp. 8-12, Tables 1-2 & Results

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Primary mixed-methods study combining a quantitative structured questionnaire component (n = 100, descriptive statistics and chi-square goodness-of-fit test) with primary qualitative components (targeted focus group discussions across 5 neighborhoods, key informant interviews, direct spot-check observations, and thematic coding of transcripts).

sample_size.comment: Fieldwork conducted October 2-18, 2024 across 5 Foumbot neighborhoods (Company, Njimbot 1, Nkouondja, Koudounbain, and Mbandjou), supplemented by key informant interviews with water vendors, residents, and community heads, direct field observations, and secondary records from Camwater and Foumbot council.
sample_size.value: 100 participants/questionnaires across 5 neighborhoods (20 randomly selected participants per neighborhood for targeted focus group discussions and structured questionnaires; plus 10 pilot respondents outside the study communities and secondary Camwater administrative data for 2,076-2,772 users from 2015-2021)
sample_size.where_found: PDF pp. 4-5, Materials and Methods; Table 1, PDF p. 9; Table 2, PDF p. 10; PDF p. 12

study_design.comment: Combines quantitative survey/chi-square analysis with qualitative focus groups, interviews, and observational thematic analysis, plus secondary utility administrative records.
study_design.value: Mixed-methods cross-sectional field study combining structured questionnaires (descriptive statistics and chi-square goodness-of-fit test) with targeted focus group discussions, key informant interviews, direct field observations (thematic analysis), and secondary administrative data review
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 4-6, Materials and Methods
